that they are Christians,
and even those who are recognized are insulted, buffeted, driven away, and stripped.
And behold, all the Christians in these regions are tormented in a chastisement such as this—
not to say abandonment—by God,
and in the midst of tempestuous waves they are tossed about and buffeted,
while the enemies of justice mock them and say to them:
"Where is your God?
Let us see if {OCR?} you have a helper,
or one who saves and delivers."
Now this persecution held sway not over our people alone,
but also over the Jews;
and over the pagan priests, the worshippers of idols, manifoldly, after that great honor which used to be set apart for them by the Mongol kings,
so that half of the revenue which was gathered in the treasuries {OCR?} of the kingdom used to be given to the pagan priests,
and was expended {OCR?} on the making of idols of gold and silver.
And because of the persecution against them,
most of the pagan priests became Muslims.
And afterwards a command went forth from the King of Kings,
and yarlighs were written to all the countries,
and Mongol envoys {OCR?} were sent to every country and city to destroy the churches and to plunder the monasteries.
And wherever the envoys went,
and a Christian was found who stood before them to serve them and give them gifts,
they were easily pacified and appeased.
Because they cared more about the gathering of mammon
than about the destruction of the churches,
just as it happened in the city of Arbela.
For when the commanders arrived there,
and remained twenty {OCR?} days,
and waited for someone from the Christians to approach,
and take upon himself a certain amount of gold,
and show generosity of hand towards them for the salvation of the churches there, so that they might not be harmed,
no one approached.
Neither did the Metropolitan who was there bear the burden of his churches,
nor did anyone else take upon himself the care of the churches,
but everyone was caring for the management of his own personal house.
Therefore, immediately an opportunity was given to the pagans,
and they stretched out {OCR?} a hand against the three splendid churches that were there,
and destroyed them completely down to the foundations.
These things happened {OCR?}
